claim: Facing is which way the body is turned, independent of where the camera sits or where the eyes go. It is the first thing a viewer reads off a character: to_camera confronts, three-quarter is the workhorse of conversation, and back withholds the face entirely.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: facing viewer, front view, body facing forward
from behind, three-quarter view, shoulder toward viewer
from behind, facing away, back turned

review.issue: Danbooru/Animagine has no reliable lateral vocabulary: "body turned left", "facing left", "facing right" are not trained tags, and the model mirrors at random. three_quarter_left vs three_quarter_right and profile_left vs profile_right will come back as two arbitrary pairs — four options, two pictures. back and back_three_quarter are both dominated by "from behind" and will read the same; "shoulder toward viewer" carries no weight against it.
review.fix: Use the tags that exist — "facing viewer", "profile" / "from side", "from behind", "facing away" — and either collapse each L/R pair into one option or keep them while stating in the claim that direction is a coin flip this model will not honour. Give back_three_quarter a real separator such as "looking back" or "looking over shoulder".
